route: Nitrate-containing Beet It Sport beetroot juice

identity.tested: Concentrated beetroot juice versus manufacturer nitrate-depleted matching juice
not_tested_as_equivalent: Unspecified beetroot, beet powder or reformulated retail products
identity.limit: The matched juice contrast supports the role of its nitrate content in that matrix. It does not establish efficacy interchangeability with isolated salts or all beet products.
identity.inventory: See identity-check.json; initial clean 235 decisions at 1aca821, later parent working snapshot 238. No repository edits.

2015.source_version: NIHMS708599 author manuscript in PMC4573847, underlying 2015 publication

participants.condition: Nonischemic systolic HF, EF≤45%, stable medication; no major other organ dysfunction or exercise contraindication. All nine took beta-blockers, seven ACE inhibitor/ARB, four spironolactone, three statin. Medication unchanged during trial.

design.randomization: Order generated online; detailed concealment not described. Subjects could not reliably identify the active visit when queried.
design.flow: Native Figure 1: six screening exclusions; among 31 eligible, 15 declined, six could not be contacted and one sustained injury; all nine enrolled completed. No post-allocation loss in this report.
design.eligibility: Antacids, proton-pump/xanthine-oxidase inhibitors and PDE inhibitors excluded; these study restrictions are not new contraindication determinations.

exposure.product: Beet It Sport, James White Drinks
exposure.duration: Single dose; exercise began two hours later, with six-minute walk followed by dynamometry
exposure.control: Same volume, nitrate depleted using an ion-exchange resin; reported matching packaging, color, texture, taste and smell. Exact residual nitrate and batch assay not supplied.
exposure.background: Low-nitrate diet for ten days before and throughout study, overnight food/caffeine/alcohol/exercise avoidance and no gum/antibacterial mouthwash on test days. These are study conditions, not advice.

statistics.model: Treatment×order ANOVA, subject repeated within treatment, alpha .05
statistics.author_named_primary: Breath NO and peak/maximal muscle power and velocity
statistics.secondary: Other outcomes including walking, isometric torque and fatigue
statistics.power: Designed to detect effect size≥.69 at 80% power with assumed within-person correlation .95
limits: No paired treatment confidence intervals supplied
Nonsignificant treatment×order interaction does not prove absence of carryover
Parabola-derived maximum power and velocity are related outputs of the measured power curve

measured_high_speed_power.interpretation: P=.07 is nonsignificant. The asterisk and caption’s significance wording do not override the numerical P.
Measured high-speed voluntary knee-extension torque multiplied by velocity gives a power benefit.

modeled_Pmax.method: Parabolic fit to the measured peak-power/velocity relation; correlated with the measured high-speed effect, not independent replication. Standard error is explicitly identified in the current registry.

later_registry_same_endpoint.test: Paired two-sided t-test in the current registry post
later_registry_same_endpoint.limit: Same values and same registered trial; not an additional 17-person power study, and not the exact P from the paper’s stated ANOVA.

modeled_Vmax.plusminus_definition: The read manuscript does not explicitly label this figure/abstract dispersion; do not silently call it SD.
modeled_Vmax.panel_locator: Native Figure 3 has velocity above power; Results prose reverses these panel locators.

isometric_torque.meaning: No detected static-strength benefit; no treatment CI supplied.

six_minute_walk.meaning: No detected walking benefit. Post hoc power calculations do not convert it to a positive.

fatigue_table4.inference: All reported comparisons null; 50 repeated contractions at 3.14 rad/s are not 50 independent participants.

outcomes.markers: Plasma nitrate and breath NO increased; plasma nitrite difference was not significant. Breath NO is a proxy, not direct muscle NO, sGC or cGMP mediation evidence.
outcomes.blood_pressure: No significant treatment difference in this acute nine-person study; no general hemodynamic equivalence claim.

harms.article: One participant reported abdominal cramping and loose stools; no significant serious clinical events and no significant BP change.
harms.current_registry: Zero other/serious/death events posted for 17 people per condition, despite the article’s GI symptom report. Preserve both; cause of discrepancy unknown.
harms.limit: No long-term, pediatric, MVA or tumor safety conclusion.

2015.mechanism: No muscle biopsy, NO-cGMP or calcium-handling mediation experiment beyond plasma nitrate/nitrite and breath NO. Voluntary dynamometry does not isolate fiber, neural or blood-flow mechanisms. No BUB1B/BubR1/checkpoint/fidelity endpoint. The authors’ one-third deficit comparison uses external healthy cohorts, not randomized normalization to a healthy range.
2015.funding: Barnes-Jewish Hospital Foundation, Washington University programs and NIH-supported UL1 TR000448; disclosures None.
2015.scope: Complete scientific author-manuscript text, four table texts and all three native figures. Linked supplemental DOCX/XML requests returned HTML challenges and were not read.

2023.version: Published paper, not predecessor preprint PMID36824817
2023.design: Secondary pooled analysis of two registered trials; randomized double-blind acute crossover comparisons with one-week washout. The published paper does not map individual contributions or overlap with the parent-trial publications.

participants.condition: Community dwelling; major cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, neuromuscular and other exercise-limiting diseases excluded. No HF/MVA/myopathy cohort.
participants.flow_limit: The eight initial-visit exclusions should not be presented as post-treatment attrition.

exposure.timing: Two hours before testing; 24-hour restriction of nitrate-rich foods and 12-hour fasting/caffeine/alcohol restriction
exposure.blinding: Independent individual assigned active/placebo to coded bottle labels; broken after data collection.

2023.assay: After a non-fatigued force-velocity protocol reported separately, participants performed 50 all-out knee extensions at 3.14 rad/s, followed by recovery measurements through ten minutes. The participant, not each contraction, is the independent unit.
2023.statistics: Repeated-measures treatment×time/repetition ANOVA, Holm–Šidák post hoc comparisons, paired t-tests for summary/fit parameters. No CIs or equivalence bounds; separate correction across all endpoint families not established.

outcomes.plasma: Reported individual-peak nitrate and nitrite increases were 21±8 and 4±4 fold; these were not reconstructed from ratios of group means. Breath NO was not measured.
outcomes.curvefit: Predicted minimum/maximum and fitted rate parameter were null. The source labels a parameter in s^-1 a time constant; no refit or half-life reconstruction was performed.
outcomes.figure_stars: Native Figures 2 and 3 mark fatigue/recovery relative to baseline, not nitrate-versus-placebo superiority.

2023.harms: No systematic adverse-event table in this article. The parent registries have different exposures and denominators; their safety records cannot become zero-harm evidence for all 18 women.
2023.mechanism: Plasma nitrate/nitrite increased but NO, blood flow, PCr and pH were not measured. No BUBR1 or chromosome-fidelity assay. The task-specific null does not negate the 2015 high-speed power signal.
2023.funding: IUPUI and NIH grants. No COI statement identified in the read scientific main; absence of a located statement is not a verified declaration of no conflicts.
2023.scope: Complete scientific main, all three table texts and all three native figures. Graphical abstract viewed but given no separate result credit.

current_registry_context.scope: Current records only; history not read. No claim of original prospective endpoint specification from current entries.

NCT01682356.power_result: Exactly the article’s 4.20±.33 versus4.74±.41 W/kg; dispersion explicitly SE; current paired two-sided P=.0153. Not new independent replication.
NCT01682356.VO2peak: Eight assessed; 21.4±2.1 versus23.0±2.3 mL/min/kg, SE, paired P=.0131. Registry context only; no full review of the later exercise paper or assumption of overlap/disjointness of endpoint subsets.
NCT01682356.timing: First posted September2012 after stated January2012 start; current last post December2024. This does not verify the original outcome hierarchy.

NCT03513302.design: Broader 14-day crossover with 14-day washout, not simply the pooled paper’s acute two-condition visit pair
NCT03513302.posted_power: Day1 placebo3.98±1.18 versus nitrate4.26±1.37 W/kg; day14 4.23±1.21 versus4.31±1.26, SD. No analysis P/CI in these posted endpoints; neither efficacy nor null inferred from means. PROMIS endpoints likewise have no posted inferential test.
NCT03513302.safety: No serious/death events; other events5/16 placebo versus4/16 nitrate. Screening findings27/47 are not drug effects. Nitrate reports two nausea/diarrhea participants; no causality/equivalence inferred.

NCT03595774.withdrawal: Two adverse-event withdrawals and two screen failures in posted flow; AE table uses only nine and reports zero, so no zero-event conclusion for all enrolled.
NCT03595774.posted_primary: Power means3.74/3.92/3.69 W/kg across placebo/low/high, overall ANOVA P=.0131; exact pairwise results absent. Velocity overall P=.0833. No dose-response or pairwise benefit declared here.
NCT03595774.record_issue: Some outcome placebo descriptions duplicate the low-dose mixture; other protocol labels also conflict. Preserve labels and do not invent repaired assignments.

current_registry_context.pooled_mapping: The parent registries currently list 11 and8 female completers; the paper reports18 pooled women without a person-level map. Do not assume one overlap or one exclusion to force reconciliation. Parent regimens are broader/different, and their publications are not independent replications of the pooled analysis.

competitive_judgment: Actual randomized human high-speed power is a substantive functional signal, closer to compensation than BUBR1 supply. Acute exposure, small sample, related fit-derived outputs, null task outcomes and no CIs/durability limit any nomination. Other nominees retain transfer limits too; no selective requirement for proven MVA efficacy and no cross-trial superiority claim.
systemic_tumor_unknowns: Long-term systemic effects, abnormal-clone/tumor outcomes and pediatric/MVA benefit are unmeasured here. NO-related hypotheses do not establish BubR1 restoration, and acute BP nulls do not establish universal safety.
source_reviewer_status: Qualified as a bounded human muscle-power research comparator; not automatically nominated
source_reviewer_optional_entry: Preparation-specific nitrate-containing beetroot juice is justified as a bounded reserve; empty automatic aliases prevent juice-to-salt, organic-nitrate or plain-beet inheritance. Root decides admission; no count promotion.

schema_correction.reason: The preserved unit is Nm/kg; endpoint is normalized to body mass, not absolute torque. Markdown already described it correctly.
schema_correction.existing_independent_review: The independent review bound to the prior source JSON remains available unchanged; this note does not claim its reapproval.
